svg.text: McCzarny recently enhanced his
opencode-sessions Stream Deck plugin by
introducing a new 'Go usage' key, allowing
users to track OpenCode Go allowance for
various windows. He also improved the accuracy
of session status reporting, ensuring 'NEEDS
INPUT' is correctly displayed when a session
awaits user interaction. A significant focus
was placed on the project's build system, which
was migrated from Rollup to esbuild and
TypeScript for faster compilation and better
dependency management. This involved pinning
TypeScript to version 5.x to resolve build
failures and later upgrading to TypeScript 7
after the build process refactor. McCzarny
updated several development dependencies and
ensured Node.js built-in modules are properly
polyfilled within the build. In his
chromium-daily-digest project, he temporarily
disabled scheduled daily and weekly summary
generation to conserve API tokens, adding a
notification banner. He adjusted the scheduling
of daily digest workflows to prevent overlaps
and tried to limit the number of summary points
generated. Additionally, he expanded the
configuration's focus areas, fixed tool calling
logic, and increased the OpenCode service
context limit to 1 million tokens. He also
raised the commits fetch limit to 2000 and
enhanced OpenCode model protocol handling.
